speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an infant with recurrent stridor and wheezing; can you describe exactly when these episodes happen, such as during feeding, crying, or lying flat?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Tracheomalacia. The combination of stridor and wheezing specifically worsening during crying, feeding, and neck flexion (the "tripod" of provocative maneuvers) in an infant is highly characteristic of tracheomalacia, likely with associated gastroesophageal reflux given the vomiting. No further questions are needed; this clinical picture is diagnostic.
